article.title: ‘They laughed at what they had done’: Ecuadorian fishermen sue US after surviving drone strike at sea
article.author: BreakThrough News
article.content: Several weeks have passed since Ecuadorian fishermen reported an attack on the high seas by US armed forces. According to the fishermen, US military personnel forcibly removed them from some of their fishing boats and then destroyed the vessels. Several even claimed that they were taken against their will to El Salvador, which later deported the Ecuadorians back to their home country. In Ecuador, the government of right-wing President Daniel Noboa (a staunch ally of Washington’s foreign policy) backed the attacks against its own citizens, claiming they belonged to criminal gangs that used the fishermen’s boats to refuel on their trips to Mexico and the United States. To date, nearly 10 vessels have been intercepted by US forces, and following the attacks, the fishermen’s families experienced moments of despair as they did not know the whereabouts of their loved ones. So far, no fishermen have been reported dead. The fishermen who were attacked have consistently denied the accusations made by the US military and the Ecuadorian government. In fact, the Ecuadorian courts ruled in their favor and acquitted them of any crime alleged by the Ecuadorian prosecutor’s office, a strong ally of the executive branch. “Once the judge reviewed the evidence presented by the prosecutor’s office, he determined that it had not been proven that these vessels and their crew hadn’t committed any illegal act. There was no crime,” said Juan Alvia, the fishermen’s attorney, at the time. Lawsuit against the Trump administration Seventeen fishermen, however, have decided to defend their honor and seek redress in the United States: they have filed a lawsuit in a federal court in Pennsylvania against US forces for attacking their vessels with drones, illegally detaining them, and even alleging acts of torture. The complaint states : “The attack, kidnapping, and torture described above occurred even though the Ecuadorian government, following a three-hour inspection, had just cleared the ship and its crew of any illegal activity.” The complaint is directed against the Donald Trump administration and accuses it of causing emotional distress, assault, bodily injury, unlawful detention, and the destruction of the fishermen’s private property. The lawsuit demands that the US government provide compensation for the damages caused and cease attacks in the Pacific and the Caribbean as soon as possible. Washington has justified the attacks by arguing that it is fighting to stop narco-terrorism in international waters, and that these operations are therefore “vital to US national interests.” However, Washington and the Pentagon deny that they were involved in the attack on one of the vessels that received the most media attention (the Negra Francisca Duarte II) on which several of the 17 fishermen were traveling. Nevertheless, if this is not the case, the question remains: which military forces, with comparable firepower and the use of high-tech drones, carried out the attack? In response to this question, the Ecuadorian fishermen maintain that the US armed forces were responsible, having attacked them with drones, resulting in two fishermen being seriously injured with severe burns to their legs, arms, and backs. After that, the plaintiffs claim , they jumped into the water and swam desperately until they came upon a “blue boat” whose crew “spoke English,” wore camouflage uniforms, and flew the US flag alongside the words “US Coast Guard.” Regarding the attackers’ attitude, the complaint states : “They laughed at what they had done and at how they had destroyed the fishing boat – a boat that provided a livelihood for all the plaintiffs.” “The violent attack … against the plaintiffs and their vessel – while they were in a vulnerable situation on the high seas and posed no threat to the US or its personnel – was extreme and outrageous; it crossed every conceivable boundary of decency and must be considered absolutely intolerable in a civilized world,” said Daniel Kovalik , the fishermen’s attorney in the United States. “[The fishermen] lost their source of income as a result of the destruction [of the boat] and are facing a serious financial crisis. They are all also suffering severe psychological trauma due to the attack and the kidnapping,” the attorney concluded . This is the second lawsuit filed against the Trump administration over alleged attacks on vessels on the high seas. In October, several relatives of two men from Trinidad and Tobago, who died in a missile attack off the coast of their country, filed a lawsuit against the US government.
